title: Specific relief: editorial notes and questions
summary: Read the surrounding notes and questions alongside the principal cases. The complete assigned pages are preserved here.
notes:
Klein v. PepsiCo, Inc.: Klein demonstrates why formation, breach, and remedy require separate analysis. It also contrasts with Walgreen’s difficult-to-measure long-term injury and Morris’s individually valued horse.

Walgreen Co. v. Sara Creek Property Co.: Walgreen explains the adequacy inquiry through the practical costs of measuring loss, enforcing an order, and negotiating a release. Economic reasoning can support specific relief as well as damages.

Commonwealth v. Cosby: This assigned remedies reading reaches back to reliance and promise enforcement. It illustrates why a course-wide concept index must cross the syllabus’s unit boundaries.
